basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 46.' and it opens '(Vers. 46.) Et dixit Jacob fratribus suis, Colligamus lapides. Et congregatis lapidibus'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 46.) Et dixit Jacob fratribus suis, Colligamus lapides. Et congregatis lapidibus fecerunt acervum, et comederunt super eum. Et vocavit illum Laban acervum testimonii, et Jacob vocavit illum acervum testis. Acervus Hebraea lingua (גל) GAL dicitur: AAD (עד) vero testimonium. Rursum lingua Syra acervus IGAR appellatur: testimonium SEDUTHA (שהדותא). Jacob igitur acervum testimonii, hoc est, GALAAD lingua appellavit Hebraea: Laban vero idipsum, id est, acervum testimonii, IGAR SEDUTHA, gentis suae sermone vocavit. Erat enim Syrus, et antiquam linguam parentum, provinciae, in qua habitabat, sermone mutaverat.
